messages:
Sophia M: heads up — noticed a p50/p95 latency bump on the mixtral-moe serving pool after yesterday's runtime kernel update :warning:
Tom H: saw it too. p95 up ~18% on mixtral-xxl-expert config around 12:20 UTC. nothing obvious in infra CPU/GPU utilization.
Jiang: attaching quick profiler snippet i grabbed from a single noisy host:
```
2026-03-17T12:21:03Z mixtral-router[pid=4211] kernel_select: chosen_kernel=matmul_q8_narrow seq_len=32 batch=16 expected_tokens=128 latency_est=6.2ms
2026-03-17T12:21:03Z mixtral-router[pid=4211] router: topk=4 entropy=0.14 expert_hits=3/4 cache_hit_ratio=0.12 eviction_rate=0.47
2026-03-17T12:21:03Z kvcache: avg_entry_life=3.1s entries_evicted=420 per_min
```
Jiang: core observation — router logits tightened (low entropy) so routing is concentrated, expert cache pressure spiked and kernel selector started picking the narrow Q8 kernels that are terrible for many small, concurrent sequences (weird heuristics).
Lena: we rolled kernel bump because it had wins on long sequences (seq>=512). but mixtral-moex has many short chats — mismatch.
Tom H: yep. kernel selector currently uses heuristic: if seq_len<64 or expected_tokens<100 => choose narrow_kernel. That heuristic is now hurting due to more small concurrent batches; narrow kernel has poor parallelism for MoE expert matmuls.
Sophia M: so root cause = router topology change -> low entropy -> expert hotness -> more small expert matmuls -> narrow kernel chosen -> higher latency.
Lena: runtime quick mitigations?
Tom H: proposals:
- revert kernel bump on mixtral-moe pool (fast)
- temporarily increase router topk to 8 or add jitter/tempering to logits to spread load (medium)
- change kernel selection rule to consider concurrent_active_experts and per-expert_batch_size before selecting narrow kernel (longer)
- adjust kvcache eviction to be LRU with higher cap for top experts (medium)
Jiang: i ran a quick A/B on a canary VM: forcing wide_kernel for seq<=64 brought p95 down ~22% on that host. but cost per-token up ~6%.
Sophia M: tradeoff is fine for now if it stabilizes customer SLAs. prefer revert+canary change then a proper heuristic fix.
infra-bot: deploy triggered by @Lena to pool mixtral-moe-canary, rollout id=rl-2026-314. started at 12:48 UTC.
Lena: I'll kick rollback of the kernel bump for the main production pool, canary first. monitor traces.
Tom H: action items:
- Lena: rollback kernel bump on prod pool -> done on canary and watch (owner)
- Jiang: instrument kernel selector to emit `concurrent_active_experts` and `per_expert_batch_size` (owner)
- Sophia: add a perf regression test in CI that runs mixtral-moe with short-chat workload (owner)
- Me(Tom): prototype heuristic: prefer wide_kernel when (concurrent_active_experts > 12 AND per_expert_batch_size < 8)
Sophia M: also add router entropy alert to SLO page — if entropy < 0.2 and p95 > baseline+10% -> page oncall.
Jiang: note on kvcache: eviction_rate spikes were correlated with expert_hotset growth. I recommend bumping top-expert cache cap from 64MB->128MB per-expert for 24h to verify impact.
Lena: rolling the canary now, will post results in 15m.
Tom H: if canary looks good, we'll push revert to prod and then follow-up with selector heuristic PR.
Sophia M: thanks team. please paste canary numbers and profiler traces here. :eyes:
infra-bot: canary rollout complete for rl-2026-314 -> 6/6 hosts healthy; metric snapshots stored: s3://redwood-perf/mixtral/canaries/2419876543/
Lena: canary p95 dropped to baseline, p50 slightly up, kvcache hit for top experts rose from .12 -> .59 after cap bump. will keep observe for 2 hours.
Tom H: opened issue: https://redwood-internal/issue/ENG-5234 "mixtral: kernel selector decoupling from routing hotness (perf regression)" — assigning to @Jiang and @Tom H.
Sophia M: nice work. long term follow-ups: i) refine kernel cost model to include expert-level concurrency, ii) add router-side soft-tempering during spikes, iii) add perf alerts for kernel-selection flips.
Lena: i'll post a short runbook to /docs/eng-runtime/mixtral-kernel-regressions after we stabilize.
Jiang: adding a microbench harness to simulate 10k short-chat concurrent requests to validate selector heuristics. will link when ready.
Sophia M: perfect. closing thread once prod revert confirmed stable. :white_check_mark:
